title: Mark my words: Tony Winner Marla Mindelle incoming #Titanique #Broadw...
transcript: Titanic is officially coming to Broadway. And I think the question on everyone's mind is why? I mean, yes, the off Broadway run was a success, but it also ran for three years. And basically everyone who has wanted to see Titanic has seen Titanic. And the reason why it closed off Broadway in the first place was because it was struggling to sell its 200 seat off Broadway theater. And now they're going into a 17 seat Broadway theater. And so I do wonder if this is more of a long term play. Which is to say, even if your show flops on Broadway, there are still ways for that show to make money. I'm not saying it definitely will flop, but I do think it is a tougher sell to Broadway audiences. However, where I don't think it's a tough sell is touring on the road and also being licensed regionally. And having the show produced on Broadway is going to give them more notoriety when doing those things. Because now it's not just Titanic, it's Broadway's Titanic. And that carries a lot of weight. It is also only a 16 week run, so it's not trying to do an open ended run for 10 years kind of run. And it is coming in a lighter season. For new musicals, we really don't have that many. So while if it came last season, I think it would have gotten completely shut out at the Tonys, I do think This year, we could see a pick up a ton of nominations and maybe even some wins. Like, in my mind, Marla Mindelle, who is playing Celine Dion, she also co wrote the show, is the front runner for Best Actress. Obviously, there's still some performances we haven't seen. There's still some shows to be announced, but based on what's announced now, I think she has a really good shot. And if that happens, then not only are you Broadway's Titanic, but you could slap Tony nominated on all of those. And so, while, yes, I do think Titanic will struggle to sell on Broadway, I do think this is a really smart move for them long term.
classificationReason: Discusses the business rationale and prospects of Titanique's Broadway transfer announcement. Creator has not seen the Broadway production; no first-hand attendance or opinion on the live show itself.
